question: What is the primary purpose of public health surveillance in nursing and healthcare?

options.A: To punish healthcare workers who miss reporting cases
options.B: The continuous collection and analysis of data for planning and evaluation
options.C: To diagnose individual patients in emergency rooms
options.D: To replace traditional clinical bedside nursing duties entirely

explanation: Public health surveillance involves the systematic, ongoing collection and interpretation of health data to guide health planning, implementation, and evaluation. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following groups is typically considered a high-risk population in the Nigerian healthcare context?

options.A: Healthy middle-aged adult males with steady employment
options.B: Internally displaced persons (IDPs) and malnourished children under five
options.C: Retired corporate executives living in urban estates
options.D: University professors with comprehensive health insurance

explanation: Internally displaced persons and malnourished children under five face significant socioeconomic and environmental vulnerabilities, placing them in high-risk groups. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h1)

question: Why is the Primary Health Care (PHC) setting ideal for identifying high-risk groups?

options.A: It has the most advanced surgical equipment in the country
options.B: It serves as the first point of contact for individuals and families
options.C: Patients are always admitted for at least two weeks
options.D: It exclusively treats rare genetic disorders

explanation: PHC is the entry point into the health system, providing nurses with direct opportunities to encounter and screen vulnerable community members. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is a behavioral indicator that flags an individual as high-risk in a PHC setting?

options.A: Consuming a balanced diet of local foods
options.B: Defaulting from chronic medication regimens like antiretrovirals
options.C: Attending all scheduled antenatal care visits early

explanation: Defaulting from chronic medication regimens is a key behavioral risk factor that can lead to disease progression and resistance. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h2)

question: What distinguishes active surveillance from passive surveillance?

options.A: Active surveillance relies on nurses proactively searching for cases, whereas passive surveillance relies on routine reporting by providers
options.B: Active surveillance is only used for non-communicable diseases
options.C: Passive surveillance requires door-to-door interviewing of every citizen
options.D: Active surveillance is illegal in primary healthcare centers

explanation: In active surveillance, health workers actively seek out cases, while passive surveillance involves clinicians routinely submitting reports of seen cases. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h3)

question: Why are standardized case definitions important in health surveillance?

options.A: They ensure that data collected across different regions can be reliably compared
options.B: They eliminate the need for any laboratory testing whatsoever
options.C: They guarantee that patients will never experience side effects
options.D: They prevent patients from changing their healthcare providers

explanation: Standardized case definitions provide uniform criteria, ensuring consistent and comparable data reporting across various healthcare facilities and locations. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is a key focus of social assessments when evaluating high-risk populations?

options.A: Measuring exact serum electrolyte levels in a laboratory
options.B: Evaluating social determinants of health like housing, food security, and income
options.C: Calculating the precise dosage of intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Assessing the structural integrity of hospital buildings

explanation: Social assessments evaluate the broader social determinants of health that significantly impact an individual's wellbeing and vulnerability. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h4)

question: Why is cultural sensitivity particularly important during assessments in Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Cultural beliefs and religious practices heavily influence health-seeking behaviors
options.B: It is a requirement to pass international licensing examinations only
options.C: Culture completely dictates a patient's genetic predisposition to disease
options.D: It replaces the need to perform physical examinations on patients

explanation: Culture and religion play major roles in shaping how individuals perceive illness and whether they seek orthodox or alternative care. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between screening and diagnostic testing?

options.A: Screening is for asymptomatic individuals at risk, while diagnostics confirm disease in symptomatic patients
options.B: Screening is performed only by physicians, while diagnostics are done by nurses
options.C: Diagnostic tests are always faster and cheaper than screening tests
options.D: Screening tests are used exclusively in surgical operating theaters

explanation: Screening targets asymptomatic or at-risk individuals for early risk identification, whereas diagnostics are deployed to confirm or rule out conditions in symptomatic patients. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h5)

question: What does the sensitivity of a screening test refer to?

options.A: How gentle the nurse is when performing the venipuncture
options.B: The ability of the test to correctly identify those who actually have the disease
options.C: The speed at which the laboratory processes the payment for the test
options.D: The emotional reaction of the patient to the screening result

explanation: Sensitivity measures a test's capacity to correctly detect individuals who possess the target condition or disease. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h5)

question: Why is accurate documentation essential in public health surveillance and clinical care?

options.A: It ensures continuity of care and accurate epidemiological statistics
options.B: It allows nurses to avoid interacting directly with patients
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will receive international funding
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal communication during shift handovers

explanation: Clear and accurate documentation prevents fragmented care and provides reliable data for public health planning and statistical analysis. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h6)

question: How should a nurse handle the ethical tension between patient confidentiality and mandatory reporting of infectious diseases?

options.A: Keep all information strictly secret and refuse to report dangerous outbreaks
options.B: Report the mandatory disease for public safety while safeguarding patient dignity and privacy
options.C: Publish the patient's name and diagnosis on social media to warn others
options.D: Destroy the patient records to protect them from any form of tracking

explanation: Nurses must balance public health safety laws regarding notifiable diseases with professional obligations to respect patient privacy and dignity. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing referral pathways in public health nursing?

options.A: To transfer patients whose needs exceed primary care capacity to higher-level facilities
options.B: To permanently discharge patients from the healthcare system
options.C: To ensure patients never leave their local community health center
options.D: To increase administrative paperwork for nursing supervisors

explanation: Referral pathways ensure that patients requiring specialized or advanced care are safely and efficiently transferred to higher-level facilities. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h7)

question: Which of the following represents a key preventive nursing intervention for high-risk populations in malaria-endemic regions?

options.A: Distribution and education on the use of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs)
options.B: Administering high-dose intravenous chemotherapy to all infants
options.C: Encouraging patients to discard all community clean water sources
options.D: Restricting patient movement outside their homes at all times

explanation: Insecticide-treated nets are a proven, targeted preventive intervention used to protect vulnerable groups from malaria transmission. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h7)
